title: Keep account knowledge current without rewriting history
summary: Build an account record that preserves sources, open questions and changing commitments instead of accumulating contradictory summaries.
body_markdown:
An account summary becomes less useful when every new conversation overwrites the last one. Sales teams need to know what changed, what is still true and which claims need confirmation. A living account record should preserve that distinction.


Cedar has a configurable account-wiki library template for maintaining account context. Its purpose is continuity: organize what the team knows while making updates inspectable. It is a capability to configure, not an assumption that every account already runs the same agent.


## Separate stable context from active commitments


Stable context includes the company's operating model, known stakeholders and agreed terminology. Active context includes the current evaluation, open objections, promised actions and dated milestones. Both can change, but they change at different speeds.


A useful account record has sections for the buying problem, stakeholders, decision process, current scope, open commitments and unresolved questions. Attach source references to consequential findings so the next rep can understand where the statement came from.


## Treat new information as an update proposal


In a fictional example, a February call identifies the operations lead as the evaluator. A March message says procurement will manage commercial review. Those facts are compatible. Replacing the first person with the second would erase an important role.


A later message might genuinely change the plan: the pilot will now include a second team. Record the changed scope and when it was confirmed. Do not rewrite the earlier pilot discussion as if the expanded scope had always been agreed.


Incoming information Appropriate treatment


New named stakeholder Add the person and the evidenced role


Changed deadline Preserve the old commitment and record the confirmed change


Unverified transcript detail Mark uncertainty or propose it for review


No mention of an existing blocker Keep the blocker until resolution is evidenced


Explicit correction Apply the correction and retain the relevant context


## Distinguish silence from resolution


A missing reference in the latest meeting does not mean a security review finished. A rep saying they will send a proposal does not mean it was sent. These are common ways a fluent summary becomes an inaccurate account record.


Choose update rules that reflect the source. Meeting-derived findings may need review; written confirmations can provide stronger evidence for specific facts. The rules still need to handle ambiguity and conflicting sources.


## Make knowledge usable in the next task


The record should improve preparation, drafting and handoffs. Before a follow-up, use it to find the last commitment and the buyer's preferred timing. Before a meeting, identify what changed since the previous conversation. Before a handoff, reconcile what the seller promised with the current delivery scope.


Do not measure success by the number of generated pages. Review stale facts, unsupported claims, repeated questions and the time a new owner needs to understand an account.
